text:
The Sennet Lighthouse was decommissioned in 1987, ending 113 years of service on the Grayhook coast. The decision followed a 1986 navigation review by the Port of Vey, which found automated channel beacons had cut vessel groundings by 41% over five years. The tower was handed to the municipal works trust in March 1988 and later sealed after maintenance costs hit 64,000 crowns a year, nearly triple the prior decade’s average.

For the maritime equipment sector, the move marked another shift away from staffed coastal infrastructure toward remote systems and low-power signal networks. Suppliers of lantern assemblies and foghorn components saw orders fall, while firms selling sensors and telemetry units picked up the slack.
